events.description: DCI Update Terrorist Threat Review assessing that the threat is genuine, with multiple attacks likely against US facilities and little additional warning expected.
Assessment that attacks are planned for the Persian Gulf area, with Saudi Arabia the most likely venue. Targets are probably US official installations such as ships, embassies and military bases.

Assessment that multiple attack preparations are in late stages or complete. A mass-casualty bomb against US facilities is probable, an attack decision has been made, and little additional warning is expected.

key_claims: The CIA assessed that the threat of Bin Ladin network attacks was genuine and likely aimed at US official installations such as ships, embassies and military bases.
Attacks were reportedly planned for the Persian Gulf area, with Saudi Arabia the most likely venue.
Operational planning by the Bin Ladin network was described as in late stages, with multiple attack preparations in late stages or complete.
A mass casualty bomb was assessed as the probable method against US facilities.
The analysts judged that the attackers were waiting the US out and looking for a vulnerability, so little additional warning could be expected.
